Wait, the diamond is (52,10,57,13): a 6x4 charcoal shape to the right of the green strip. In Level 1 the diamond was 6 wide, 4 tall (charcoal) and the yellow strip was 2 wide, 4 tall. This time the strip is green N (12 px: 4 rows x … bbox (52,8,57,9) = 4 rows x 2 cols… wait rows 52-57 = 6 rows? No: bbox rows 52-57, but 12 px over 6 rows x 2 cols = shape of 4 tall? bbox row range: min 52 max 57 → 6 rows. 12 px / 2 cols = 6 rows… but Level 1's strip was a full 6x2=12. Yeah, complete 6x2.
Hmm wait, Level 1: the Y strip's bbox is (28,38,31,39) = 4 rows x 2 cols = 8 px; the one at (44,50,49,51) = 6 rows x 2 cols = 12 px. Right.
Here N strip (52,8,57,9): 6x2=12. c diamond (52,10,57,13): 6 rows x 4 cols = 16 px (diamond shape). Green gap on bar 2: (40,28,43,29) 4 rows x 2 cols = 8 px.
So the shape is the same: a diamond-piece with a strip attached, and on the bar there's a gap the size of the strip. This time the gap is green and the strip is also green (color match!). In Level 1, gap is yellow, strip is yellow, diamond is charcoal. Blue squares: this time on the left edge, arranged vertically: rows 16-19 (above bar 1, on the left), rows 24-27 (between the bars, on the left), rows 36-39 (between the bars, on the left), rows 44-47 (below bar 2, on the left). Four blue squares: two above bar 1?? No: rows 16-19 are above bar 1 (20-23). Rows 24-27: directly below bar 1 (inside the intermediate white pocket). Rows 36-39: above bar 2 (40-43). Rows 44-47: below bar 2 (inside the bottom pocket).
So the bars run horizontally (in Level 1 they ran vertically? no, the bar in Level 1 was also horizontal, rows 28-31, and the blue was on the right edge above and below the bar). Here the bar is horizontal, the blue is on the left edge above and below each bar. Presumably clicking a blue shifts the strip's assembly ±4 in the horizontal direction (same direction as Level 1, but perhaps the blue for each bar controls which bar moves? Or the whole mechanism?).
The gap moves with the bar? In Level 1 the bar and gap were fixed, and the strip moved. Here too presumably the bar/gap is fixed and the strip/diamond moves ±4 per click; the white boundary shifts.
Goal (from Level 1): align the strip's column with the gap's column → strip is cols 8-9; gap is cols 28-29. The strip needs +20 → 5 clicks of +4. Which blue gives +4? In Level 1, the blue above the bar (right) gave +4 (rightward = the direction of the edge of…). Hmm. In Level 1's orientation the blue was on the right and the assembly moved right with the "upper" blue. Here the blue is on the left; maybe the assembly moves left with one blue and right with the other. Or the mechanism: the "upper" blue (the one pointing more upward/away) = strip goes in the direction of…, hmm.
Also, which bar? There are two bars but only one gap (on bar 2). Bar 1 (20-23) has no gap — a solid 224 px? 224 = 4 rows x 56 cols → cols 0-55, solid, no gap. Bar 2 has a green gap.
The four blues: maybe there are two pairs: pair A (rows 16-19 and 24-27) flanks bar 1; pair B (rows 36-39 and 44-47) flanks bar 2. In Level 1 the pair flanked the single bar. Probably clicking a blue shifts the assembly: one direction or the other; level has two gaps total? No, there's only one gap.
Hmm, Level 2's twist may be: clicking a blue shifts the assembly, and additionally each blue pair controls which bar/pocket the edges of the gray/white shift for? In Level 1: upper blue shift → upper white edge -4, lower white edge +4, assembly +4 (right).
The piece here is at the bottom (rows 52-57, cols 8-13), fixed to the bottom white edge: bottom white cols 0-7, strip at cols 8-9 (rightmost of the white! In Level 1 the strip was on the gray side, adjacent to the white's left edge. Here the white is a left pocket (cols 0-7) and the strip is cols 8-9 = right side of the white's right edge). The diamond is 10-13, on the gray.
So presumably the assembly moves right to align the strip's cols with the gap's cols 28-29. Strip is cols 8-9 → needs +20 → 5 clicks.
But which blue gives +4? Unclear. Candidates: the blue at (44-47,0-3) is below bar 2, on the left — by symmetry with Level 1 (lower blue = -4 there). The one above bar 1 (16-19) = +? In Level 1 the "upper" blue gave +4. If the pattern holds by position relative to the bar, then the blue above the bar = +4. But which bar's blue affects the assembly? Or do all four do the same shift? The two middle blues (24-27, 36-39) are on the opposite side of the bar from the edges.
Efficient exploration: click the blue at (45,1) (below bar 2) and check the strip position. If the strip goes 12 (left, -4) and the bottom white grows… then the opposite blue (above bar 2 at (37,1)) should give +4. But careful: each exploration costs 1 timer tick. Timer is full at 64. Level 1 required 5 clicks; here I estimate ~5-7 clicks. No problem.
But note: maybe clicking a blue only shifts the local pocket's edge and its opposite side, and only works if the piece is "attached" to that pocket. The piece is inside the bottom pocket (rows 44-63, white cols 0-7). The two blues flanking bar 2 are (36-39) above and (44-47) below. The middle blues (16-19, 24-27) flank bar 1 and may control the upper/middle pocket (moving the upper white edge or the middle white edge) — irrelevant to the piece?? Or maybe clicking any blue shifts the whole mechanism.
Exploration: click (45,1) [below bar 2]. Observe the strip/white.
